x: Ants live in big groups. Their home is called a colony. Some ants dig tunnels, and some ants look for food. When an ant finds a crumb, it tells the other ants. Then they all come to help. I saw two ants carry a leaf that was bigger than them. Ants are small, but they are very strong.

My dog Max likes to run in the park. Every morning, we go there with Mom. Max chases the ball, and I throw it again. He wags his tail when he is happy. After our walk, Max drinks lots of water. Then he takes a long nap on his bed. I love my dog, and he loves me too.

A frog starts as a tiny egg in a pond. The egg hatches into a tadpole. A tadpole has a tail and swims like a fish. Soon it grows back legs, and then it grows front legs. Its tail gets shorter and shorter. At last, it hops out of the water as a frog. Frogs eat bugs, flies, and worms.

Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings to swim fast in the sea. Many penguins live where it is very cold. Their feathers keep them warm and dry. Some penguin dads keep an egg warm on their feet. I saw penguins at the zoo, and they waddled to the water. Then they jumped in and swam away.

Ice is water that is very cold. When ice gets warm, it melts. Then it turns back into water. I put an ice cube in a cup on a sunny day. After a little while, the cube was gone. There was only water in the cup. We can put the water in the freezer, and it will be ice again.

Our class planted bean seeds in cups. We gave them water, soil, and sunlight. After a week, a small green sprout came up. Sam forgot to water his cup, so his seed did not grow. Plants need water to live. Now Sam waters his cup every day, and his bean is growing too.

We have five senses. We see with our eyes and hear with our ears. We smell with our nose and taste with our tongue. We touch things with our skin. At lunch, I used all five senses. I saw a red apple, and I smelled it. Then I bit it and heard a crunch. It tasted sweet, and it felt smooth.

A magnet can pull some things to it. Magnets stick to things made of iron, like nails and paper clips. They do not stick to paper, wood, or plastic. My teacher gave us a magnet to test. I tried a paper clip, a crayon, and a block. The paper clip stuck, but the crayon and the block did not.

The Sun is a star. It is the closest star to Earth. It looks small in the sky because it is very far away. The Sun gives us light and heat. Plants need its light to grow. Never look right at the Sun, because it can hurt your eyes. At night, we can see other stars, but they are much farther away.

Long ago, in 1969, people walked on the Moon for the first time. Their names were Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin. They flew there in a spaceship. The Moon has no air, so they wore space suits. They picked up rocks and took pictures. Then they flew back home to Earth.

Earth spins around and around. It takes one day to spin all the way. When our side of Earth faces the Sun, it is day. When our side faces away, it is night. I go to school in the day. At night, I look at the stars with my mom. Then I brush my teeth, and I go to bed.

Last summer, I went camping with my family. At night, we lay on a big blanket. The sky was dark, and there were many stars. Dad showed me the Big Dipper. It looks like a giant spoon. My sister saw the Moon, and she waved at it. We counted stars until we fell asleep.

It rained all day on Monday. Big gray clouds filled the sky. I wore my boots and my yellow coat. On the way to school, I jumped in a puddle. Rain gives plants and animals the water they need. After school, the sun came out. Then I saw a rainbow over the hill. It had red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

Rocks are all around us. Some rocks are big, and some are small. Some are smooth, and some are rough. I keep a box of rocks in my room. I found a white rock at the beach and a black rock by a river. My favorite rock is shiny. Mom says the shiny bits are crystals.

Oceans are very big and very deep. Their water is salty, so we cannot drink it. Fish, crabs, and whales live in the ocean. There is also a tall seaweed called kelp. When I went to the beach, I saw waves crash on the sand. I found two shells and a starfish. I put the starfish back in the water.

There are four seasons in a year. They are spring, summer, fall, and winter. In spring, flowers bloom and birds sing. Summer is hot, so we swim in the lake. In fall, the leaves turn red and drop down. Winter can be cold and snowy. My favorite season is winter, because I like to build a snowman.

The flag of the United States has stars and stripes. It has 13 stripes for the first 13 states. It has 50 stars, one for each state today. The colors are red, white, and blue. Long ago, the flag had only 13 stars. Our class has a flag by the window, and we look at it every morning.

George Washington was the first president of the United States. He lived on a farm in Virginia called Mount Vernon. He liked to ride horses. Today his face is on the one dollar bill and the quarter. The city of Washington, D.C., is named after him. I saw his picture in my book, and he had white hair.

Long ago, children did not have toys with batteries. They played with wooden tops, dolls, and marbles. Some kids made their own toys from sticks and string. My grandma played jump rope with her friends. She showed me how to play, and I jumped ten times. Old games are still fun to play today.

Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States. He grew up in a small log cabin. He loved to read books, and he read by the light of the fire. He was very tall, and he often wore a tall black hat. His face is on the penny. I have a penny in my pocket right now.

People say hello in many ways. In Mexico, people say hola. In France, they say bonjour. In Japan, people may bow to say hello. In the United States, we often wave or shake hands. My friend Mia speaks two languages. She taught me to say hello in Spanish, and now I say hola to her every day.

A map is a drawing of a place. It shows where things are. Our class made a map of our town. We drew the school, the park, and the library. I drew the river in blue. Jake drew the roads in black. A map can help you find your way. Then you will not get lost.

Canada is a country north of the United States. It is very big. Its flag is red and white, and it has a red maple leaf. Many people in Canada speak English, and some speak French. My uncle lives in Canada. When we visited him, we saw snow, lakes, and tall trees.

Earth has seven continents. They are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. We live in North America. Asia is the biggest continent. Antarctica is the coldest, and it is covered with ice. Penguins live there, but very few people do.

On my first day of school, I felt a little shy. My mom walked me to the door. My teacher, Mrs. Lee, smiled and said hello. I sat next to a boy named Ben. We drew pictures, read a book, and played outside. At lunch, Ben shared his grapes with me. By the end of the day, I had a new friend.

Here is how to make a jam sandwich. First, get two slices of bread. Next, spread jam on one slice. Then put the other slice on top. Cut it in half, so it is easy to hold. Now your sandwich is ready to eat. I like to make one for my little brother, and he says it is yummy.

I help my family at home. Every day, I make my bed and feed our cat. On Saturday, I help Dad wash the dishes. My sister sweeps the floor, and I put away the toys. When we all help, the work goes fast. Then we have time to play a game together.

Today is my birthday, and I am seven. My friends came to my house for a party. We played games and ate cake. The cake was chocolate with blue frosting. I blew out all the candles at once. Then I opened my gifts. My grandpa gave me a kite. We flew it in the yard.

Soccer is a fun game. Two teams try to kick a ball into a net. You cannot use your hands, but the goalie can. On Saturday, I played soccer with my team. I ran fast and kicked the ball. It went into the net, and everyone cheered. After the game, we had orange slices.

This summer, I learned how to swim. At first, I was scared of the deep water. My coach, Mr. Diaz, showed me how to kick my legs. Then I learned to move my arms. I practiced every day at the pool. Now I can swim all the way across. I am proud of myself.

At recess, we like to play tag. One kid is it. That kid runs and tries to tag the others. If you get tagged, then you are it. Lily is very fast, so it is hard to tag her. I hid behind the slide, but Omar found me. We played until the bell rang.

I got a new bike for my birthday. It is red with a silver bell. At first, I used training wheels. Then my dad took them off. He held the seat while I rode. I wobbled, but I did not fall. Now I ride my bike to the park. I always wear my helmet to keep my head safe.

Red, yellow, and blue are called primary colors. You can mix them to make new colors. Red and yellow make orange. Blue and yellow make green. Red and blue make purple. In art class, I mixed paint on a plate. I painted a green tree and an orange sun. My teacher hung it on the wall.

Our class put on a play about three little pigs. I was the wolf, and I wore a gray mask. Ella, Max, and Rosa were the pigs. We practiced our lines for two weeks. On the big day, our families came to watch. I was nervous, but I said all my lines. At the end, everyone clapped.

Music can be loud or soft. It can be fast or slow. In music class, we play drums, bells, and shakers. I like the drum best, because it goes boom. My friend Kim plays the bells. When we play together, it sounds like a song. Then we sing, and our teacher plays the piano.

On Friday, our class went to the library. There were so many books on the shelves. I found a book about sharks, and Leo found a book about trucks. The librarian read us a story about a lost duck. Then we got to check out books. I took my book home and read it to my dad.

The wheel is a very old invention. People made wheels thousands of years ago. Wheels help us move heavy things. Cars, bikes, and buses all have wheels. A wagon has four wheels. I pull my little sister in our wagon. It is much easier than carrying her!

Long ago, Alexander Graham Bell made one of the first telephones. With a telephone, people can talk to someone far away. The first phones were big, and they hung on the wall. Today, many phones are small enough to fit in a pocket. I call my grandma on the phone every Sunday. She tells me jokes, and I laugh.

A light bulb helps us see at night. Long ago, people used candles and oil lamps. Then Thomas Edison and other inventors worked on light bulbs. Edison made a bulb that could glow for a long time. Now we just flip a switch, and the room gets bright. I have a small lamp by my bed.

An umbrella keeps you dry in the rain. It opens up like a big flower. The top is made of cloth that water cannot get through. The rain rolls off the edges. When the rain stops, you close it up. I have a green umbrella with frogs on it. I take it to school on rainy days.
